/-!
# Woodin's question: GCH below a strongly compact cardinal

Woodin asked whether the generalized continuum hypothesis (GCH) below a strongly compact
cardinal implies GCH everywhere. That is, if $\kappa$ is strongly compact and
$2^\lambda = \lambda^+$ for every infinite cardinal $\lambda < \kappa$, must
$2^\lambda = \lambda^+$ hold for every infinite cardinal $\lambda$?

An uncountable cardinal $\kappa$ is *strongly compact* if every $\kappa$-complete filter
(on any set) can be extended to a $\kappa$-complete ultrafilter. Mathlib does not define
strongly compact cardinals, so this file defines them in terms of `CardinalInterFilter`.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, W. Hugh Woodin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W._Hugh_Woodin)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Strongly compact cardinal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strongly_compact_cardinal)
- A. Kanamori, *The Higher Infinite*, Chapter 1, §4 (strongly compact cardinals)
- T. Jech, *Set Theory*, 3rd millennium edition, Chapter 20 (strongly compact cardinals)
-/

blocks.docstring:
A cardinal `κ` is *strongly compact* if it is uncountable and, for every type `S` (in the
same universe as `κ`), every proper `κ`-complete filter on `S` extends to a `κ`-complete
ultrafilter on `S`. Here a filter is `κ`-complete if it is closed under intersections of
fewer than `κ` of its members, see `CardinalInterFilter`.

The uncountability requirement is part of the standard definition: every proper filter
extends to an ultrafilter, so `ℵ₀` would otherwise satisfy the extension property trivially.
Since Mathlib's `Filter` includes the improper filter `⊥`, the filter to be extended is
required to be `NeBot`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Cardinal.IsInaccessible`, `Cardinal.IsRegular`, `Cardinal.IsStrongLimit` (far weaker large-cardinal notions, not equivalent); `CardinalInterFilter` (used as the κ-completeness component); `CountableInterFilter` (only ℵ₁-completeness).
justification.name: Woodin.IsStronglyCompact
justification.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib defines strongly compact (or measurable/supercompact) cardinals. Defined via the standard filter-extension characterization (Jech, Set Theory, Ch. 20; Kanamori, The Higher Infinite, §4; Wikipedia): κ is uncountable and, for every type S in the same universe, every proper (`NeBot`) κ-complete filter on S (`CardinalInterFilter F κ`) extends to a κ-complete ultrafilter on S (`∃ U : Ultrafilter S, ↑U ≤ F ∧ CardinalInterFilter ↑U κ`). Two small provable declarations (`IsStronglyCompact.aleph0_lt`, category API; `not_isStronglyCompact_aleph0`, category test) exercise the definition.

blocks.name: IsStronglyCompact
blocks.text:
/--
A cardinal `κ` is *strongly compact* if it is uncountable and, for every type `S` (in the
same universe as `κ`), every proper `κ`-complete filter on `S` extends to a `κ`-complete
ultrafilter on `S`. Here a filter is `κ`-complete if it is closed under intersections of
fewer than `κ` of its members, see `CardinalInterFilter`.

The uncountability requirement is part of the standard definition: every proper filter
extends to an ultrafilter, so `ℵ₀` would otherwise satisfy the extension property trivially.
Since Mathlib's `Filter` includes the improper filter `⊥`, the filter to be extended is
required to be `NeBot`.
-/
def IsStronglyCompact (κ : Cardinal.{u}) : Prop :=
  ℵ₀ < κ ∧ ∀ (S : Type u) (F : Filter S), F.NeBot → CardinalInterFilter F κ →
    ∃ U : Ultrafilter S, (U : Filter S) ≤ F ∧ CardinalInterFilter (U : Filter S) κ

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem IsStronglyCompact.aleph0_lt {κ : Cardinal.{u}} (h : IsStronglyCompact κ) : ℵ₀ < κ :=
  h.1
blocks.docstring: A strongly compact cardinal is uncountable.
blocks.name: IsStronglyCompact.aleph0_lt
blocks.text:
/-- A strongly compact cardinal is uncountable. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem IsStronglyCompact.aleph0_lt {κ : Cardinal.{u}} (h : IsStronglyCompact κ) : ℵ₀ < κ :=
  h.1

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem not_isStronglyCompact_aleph0 : ¬ IsStronglyCompact (ℵ₀ : Cardinal.{u}) :=
  fun h ↦ lt_irrefl _ h.aleph0_lt

blocks.text:
/-- `ℵ₀` is not strongly compact. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem not_isStronglyCompact_aleph0 : ¬ IsStronglyCompact (ℵ₀ : Cardinal.{u}) :=
  fun h ↦ lt_irrefl _ h.aleph0_lt

@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem woodin : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ κ : Cardinal.{u}, IsStronglyCompact κ →
      (∀ μ < κ, ℵ₀ ≤ μ → 2 ^ μ = Order.succ μ) →
      ∀ μ : Cardinal.{u}, ℵ₀ ≤ μ → 2 ^ μ = Order.succ μ := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Woodin's question.** Does the generalized continuum hypothesis below a strongly compact
cardinal imply the generalized continuum hypothesis everywhere?

That is, for every strongly compact cardinal $\kappa$: if $2^\lambda = \lambda^+$ for every
infinite cardinal $\lambda < \kappa$, then $2^\lambda = \lambda^+$ for every infinite
cardinal $\lambda$. All cardinals are taken in a single universe `u`.

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question: for every strongly compact cardinal κ, if 2^λ = λ⁺ for all infinite cardinals λ < κ then 2^λ = λ⁺ for all infinite cardinals λ; GCH quantifies over infinite cardinals only, 'strongly compact' is not in Mathlib and needs a definition (e.g. every κ-complete filter extends to a κ-complete ultrafilter, or fine κ-complete ultrafilters on P_κ(λ) for all λ ≥ κ), the cardinals should live in a single universe, and the intended meaning is ZFC-provability of the implication, which the Lean Prop approximates as usual for this repository.
claims.reviewer_why: c04 states exactly the intended reading: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ κ : Cardinal.{u}, IsStronglyCompact κ → (∀ μ < κ, ℵ₀ ≤ μ → 2 ^ μ = Order.succ μ) → ∀ μ, ℵ₀ ≤ μ → 2 ^ μ = Order.succ μ, with all cardinals and filter carrier types in one universe. Its bespoke IsStronglyCompact is the textbook (Jech/Kanamori/Wikipedia) filter-extension definition: ℵ₀ < κ plus every proper (NeBot) κ-complete filter (Mathlib's CardinalInterFilter) on any S : Type u extends to a κ-complete ultrafilter, with 'extends' correctly rendered as ↑U ≤ F in Mathlib's order. I verified in Lean that 2 ^ μ is cardinal exponentiation, Order.succ μ is the successor cardinal, and ↑U ≤ F ↔ ∀ s ∈ F, s ∈ U. c02/c03/c06 are essentially equivalent (c01 too, with instance-implicit binders); c04 chosen for the cleanest definition plus docstrings, references (Jech, Kanamori, Wikipedia 'Strongly compact cardinal') and API/test lemmas. c07/c08 are also faithful but re-implement κ-completeness instead of reusing Mathlib's CardinalInterFilter. c05 is REJECTED as unfaithful: it omits ℵ₀ < κ, and I proved in Lean that its IsStronglyCompact ℵ₀ holds, so its statement collapses to 'GCH holds outright'. File compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.

context: William Hugh Woodin (born April 23, 1955) is an American mathematician at Harvard University specializing in set theory. He has made many notable contributions to the theory of inner models and determinacy. A type of large cardinals, the Woodin cardinals, bears his name. In 2023, he was elected to the National Academy of Sciences.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single-slot decomposition and its notes (infinite cardinals only, strict bound below κ, one universe, bespoke strongly-compact definition, ZFC-provability approximated by a Lean Prop) match the statement and were followed.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Woodin's question: GCH below a strongly compact cardinal

Woodin asked whether the generalized continuum hypothesis (GCH) below a strongly compact
cardinal implies GCH everywhere. That is, if $\kappa$ is strongly compact and
$2^\lambda = \lambda^+$ for every infinite cardinal $\lambda < \kappa$, must
$2^\lambda = \lambda^+$ hold for every infinite cardinal $\lambda$?

An uncountable cardinal $\kappa$ is *strongly compact* if every $\kappa$-complete filter
(on any set) can be extended to a $\kappa$-complete ultrafilter. Mathlib does not define
strongly compact cardinals, so this file defines them in terms of `CardinalInterFilter`.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, W. Hugh Woodin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W._Hugh_Woodin)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Strongly compact cardinal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strongly_compact_cardinal)
- A. Kanamori, *The Higher Infinite*, Chapter 1, §4 (strongly compact cardinals)
- T. Jech, *Set Theory*, 3rd millennium edition, Chapter 20 (strongly compact cardinals)
-/

universe u

namespace Woodin

open Cardinal

/--
A cardinal `κ` is *strongly compact* if it is uncountable and, for every type `S` (in the
same universe as `κ`), every proper `κ`-complete filter on `S` extends to a `κ`-complete
ultrafilter on `S`. Here a filter is `κ`-complete if it is closed under intersections of
fewer than `κ` of its members, see `CardinalInterFilter`.

The uncountability requirement is part of the standard definition: every proper filter
extends to an ultrafilter, so `ℵ₀` would otherwise satisfy the extension property trivially.
Since Mathlib's `Filter` includes the improper filter `⊥`, the filter to be extended is
required to be `NeBot`.
-/
def IsStronglyCompact (κ : Cardinal.{u}) : Prop :=
  ℵ₀ < κ ∧ ∀ (S : Type u) (F : Filter S), F.NeBot → CardinalInterFilter F κ →
    ∃ U : Ultrafilter S, (U : Filter S) ≤ F ∧ CardinalInterFilter (U : Filter S) κ

/-- A strongly compact cardinal is uncountable. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem IsStronglyCompact.aleph0_lt {κ : Cardinal.{u}} (h : IsStronglyCompact κ) : ℵ₀ < κ :=
  h.1

/-- `ℵ₀` is not strongly compact. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem not_isStronglyCompact_aleph0 : ¬ IsStronglyCompact (ℵ₀ : Cardinal.{u}) :=
  fun h ↦ lt_irrefl _ h.aleph0_lt

/--
**Woodin's question.** Does the generalized continuum hypothesis below a strongly compact
cardinal imply the generalized continuum hypothesis everywhere?

That is, for every strongly compact cardinal $\kappa$: if $2^\lambda = \lambda^+$ for every
infinite cardinal $\lambda < \kappa$, then $2^\lambda = \lambda^+$ for every infinite
cardinal $\lambda$. All cardinals are taken in a single universe `u`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem woodin : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ κ : Cardinal.{u}, IsStronglyCompact κ →
      (∀ μ < κ, ℵ₀ ≤ μ → 2 ^ μ = Order.succ μ) →
      ∀ μ : Cardinal.{u}, ℵ₀ ≤ μ → 2 ^ μ = Order.succ μ := by
  sorry

end Woodin

items: Strongly compact is defined via the filter-extension characterization rather than L_{κκ}-compactness or fine measures on P_κ(λ); these are equivalent in ZFC for uncountable κ and the filter version maps directly onto Mathlib's `CardinalInterFilter` and `Ultrafilter`.

The definition requires `ℵ₀ < κ`. This is part of the standard definition and essential here: every proper filter extends to an ultrafilter, so ℵ₀ would otherwise be 'strongly compact', and since GCH below ℵ₀ is vacuous the conjecture would collapse to 'GCH holds outright'.

The filter to be extended is required to be `F.NeBot`, because Mathlib's `Filter` includes the improper filter `⊥` (set-theoretic filters are proper by definition); without this no cardinal could be strongly compact. The extension is expressed as `(U : Filter S) ≤ F`, which in Mathlib's order means F ⊆ U.

No regularity clause is included: in ZFC an uncountable singular κ cannot satisfy the extension property (κ-complete filters would then be κ⁺-complete, making the successor κ⁺ measurable), so the definition agrees with the standard notion.

'GCH below κ' is read as `2^λ = λ⁺` for all infinite λ strictly less than κ; GCH at κ itself is part of the conclusion, not the hypothesis. Successor cardinal is `Order.succ` on `Cardinal`; infinite means `ℵ₀ ≤ λ`.

All cardinals and the types S carrying filters live in a single universe `u`; `Type u` plays the role of the set-theoretic universe. As usual for this repository, the ZFC-provability of the implication is approximated by the Lean Prop; in particular the statement is vacuously true in any universe with no strongly compact cardinal, which is the standard limitation of this approximation.

The Wikipedia article on W. Hugh Woodin (the required reference) is biographical and does not restate the conjecture, so the precise formulation follows the list entry and the standard textbook definitions (Jech Ch. 20, Kanamori §4), which are cited in the module docstring.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguities: (1) 'GCH below κ' read as 2^λ = λ⁺ for all infinite λ strictly < κ (κ itself is in the conclusion, not the hypothesis) — standard usage. (2) The source's intended meaning is ZFC-provability of the implication; as usual in this repository it is approximated by the Lean Prop, universally quantified over strongly compact κ in Cardinal.{u}; the Prop is vacuously true in a universe with no strongly compact cardinal, but Lean cannot prove non-existence (assuming consistency of large cardinals), so the statement is not trivially decidable. (3) Regularity of κ is not assumed in the definition; it follows in ZFC (and in Lean's type theory) from uncountability + the extension property (a singular κ with the property would make κ⁺ measurable), matching Jech/Kanamori. (4) Strong compactness is defined relative to universe u (filters on types in Type u), i.e. κ is 'strongly compact in V_{λ_u}'; this is the standard limitation of modelling set-theoretic universes with Lean universes. c05 omitted ℵ₀ < κ, which I verified makes ℵ₀ strongly compact and the conjecture degenerate to plain GCH; all other candidates avoided this. c04's file is shipped unchanged.
